race: Formula 1 Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Welcome back to The Race Weekend Podcast, and Qatar is about to get properly spicy with the title still swinging wide.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Because we are deep into the season, and every point in this fight is suddenly a headline and a talking point everywhere.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: This is the weekend preview, so we are not reading a table, we are explaining why the data points exactly where it does.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Start with Max, who has been loud about George, and the headline says Russell is living rent free in his head already.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: He called Russell so far below his level, and that is exactly the kind of fuel Max thrives on into a big weekend and the crowd.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: It is also a track Max loves, so the noise, the form, and the history all line up in his favour this weekend again.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Ferrari are the other big story, with Hamilton and Leclerc chasing the same points and the same podium all weekend.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That collision is still bouncing around, and Ferrari say it is completely unacceptable for this team right now and it needs fixing.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: So the question is whether that partnership can stay sharp when the title gets close and the nerves get high on the track.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Williams have also exceeded the cost cap by six hundred and twenty seven thousand pounds, which is messy but not race stopping.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is a background headache, but the BBC will be covering the weekend, and the racing still matters most to the fans.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Top three, and I am putting Kimi Antonelli first with high confidence, because his form is right now and very hard to ignore.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I agree, because he is the championship leader, and his recent wins and consistency are hard to ignore this week, and the team knows it.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Recent wins and consistency make him the pick, even if his Qatar history is thin and not full of trophies yet.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: His one race there is an average fifth, best fifth, no podium, so we are betting on momentum over memory for this weekend.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Then Max Verstappen is second, and that is the easiest pick on the board, with high confidence attached to the data.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Three races here, average first, best first, three podiums, and strong late form with wins to keep him hot at the right time.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He has been a constant amid the chaos, and Qatar feels like his second home on a long calendar this season right now.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Now George Russell third is the one that makes me smile, because the Mercedes is fast and the history is good on paper.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: His Qatar average is fourth point seven, his best is fourth, but he has no podium here yet, and that matters for a win.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: His recent ninth is a red flag, but if he cleans it up, he is the man who can break the top two on a good day and maybe more, and that would be huge.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Deep cut time, I want Pierre Gasly in the top ten, and this is my low confidence gamble of the weekend and I own it.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Why Gasly, Jake, and why is this a low confidence gamble rather than a sure thing?

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He has been scoring points, he recently finished fifth, and Alpine can be sneaky at Qatar when it suits them on the night.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The rest of the top ten is tight, with Hamilton, Leclerc, Norris, Piastri, Hadjar and Lawson all fighting for points and positions.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: So the full top ten in order is Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, and Pierre Gasly, and that is the order.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is our preview, and this weekend could swing the title, so keep it close and enjoy the ride from the pit wall and the stakes, because it is close.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Same time next week, and let the lights go out in Qatar with the whole grid on the edge of their seats this time, and maybe the title changes.
